societies.name: Star Wars: The Mandalorian — Plazir-15
societies.society: Plazir-15’s organic citizens under the elected Duchess and Captain Bombardier

scope.period: The established post-Imperial order during Guns for Hire
scope.population: Organic residents; human citizens are the principal population proxy
exclusions: The galaxy as a homogeneous economy

societies.description:
Plazir-15 is a clear leisure society: rehabilitated droids provide so much everyday service that citizens resist switching them off because they would have to resume the work themselves. That supports strong material provision without ordinary employment. The elected Duchess and Captain Bombardier preside over a direct democracy, so the control estimate favors shared organic authority, while allowing for concentrated management of the droid fleet. This is a local arrangement, not a description of the entire New Republic.

The nonworking estimate is high but deliberately below total leisure. Ugnaught technicians maintain the droids, administrators remain active, and useful artistic or civic projects also count as work. The best guess is therefore about people participating in useful activity, rather than the amount of menial labor automated. Droid consent is compromised by the alternative of scrapping; their service is not evidence that all sentient beings have escaped labor.

guarantees.basis: Droid-provided daily services and resistance to resuming work support a strong, locally scoped floor.

control.basis: Direct democratic oversight supports shared control; fleet ownership is not specified.

nonworking.basis: Editorial all-organic-population estimate: a minority of maintainers and other useful workers, plus broader art/civic activity; not a canon statistic.

societies.name: Star Wars — Coruscant’s droid economy

scope.continuity: Screen canon, late Republic and early Empire
scope.period: Ordinary civilian life before the final Imperial collapse
scope.population: Organic residents, with humans as the principal depicted group

societies.description:
Coruscant combines extensive droid service with recognizable jobs, private advantage and deep differences between its upper levels and underworld. It belongs here as an interpretive zero variant: technical labor-saving capacity exists, yet ordinary residents still live within an economy organized around employment, status and access. The weak guarantee score is a best guess from that inequality, not a claim that the films publish a complete welfare code. The city should not inherit Plazir-15’s explicitly depicted leisure system.

Control stays near concentrated organic authority because bureaucracies, political leaders and commercial owners direct the infrastructure. Droid autonomy does not make those owners irrelevant. The modest nonworking estimate allows dependents and excluded residents while assuming much of the adult population still contributes through paid work, informal services or care. It does not treat every background crowd as unemployed. This classification describes preserved labor alongside automation, without inventing a deliberate policy to protect jobs.

guarantees.basis: Visible stratification supports weak general guarantees; exact welfare eligibility is unknown.

control.basis: Political and commercial organic institutions concentrate control, despite some representative mechanisms.

nonworking.basis: Best guess for all-age organic participation: widespread work with a substantial dependent/nonemployed minority; no lore census.

societies.name: Star Wars: Andor — Narkina 5

scope.period: The functioning prison before the mass escape

societies.description:
Narkina 5 makes the technological choice unusually explicit: the Empire uses prisoners because people can be cheaper and easier to replace than droids. This is a zero variant based on coercive cost cutting, rather than a lack of machines. Inmates perform genuinely useful manufacturing under punishing quotas. Their food and shelter maintain the labor force, but access is captive, conditional and expendable, so the guarantee coordinate remains strongly unfavorable despite routine rations.

Imperial command holds productive control; prisoners neither own the factory nor decide whether to work. The nonworking estimate is close to zero within this deliberately narrow adult cohort, with a small allowance for illness and temporary incapacity. Twelve-hour shifts do not imply that half the prisoners are nonworking: participation concerns whether they work at all. The record does not claim that their labor is technically useless, or that every Imperial industry could be replaced instantly at no cost.

guarantees.basis: Subsistence serves coercive production; illness and punishment make access precarious.

control.basis: Imperial command exercises concentrated human control.

nonworking.basis: Nearly all captive adults are assigned useful shifts; a small editorial allowance covers temporary inability to work.

societies.name: Marvel Cinematic Universe — Wakanda

scope.continuity: MCU Black Panther, not Earth-616 comics
scope.period: The established national order around T’Challa’s return, before the succession crisis

societies.description:
Wakanda pairs extraordinary technology with ordinary human occupations, craft, commerce, scientific work and farming. Its inclusion is an openly interpretive zero variant: vibranium-based engineering suggests room to reduce necessary labor further, while the society shown still values and organizes human contribution. This is not a claim that the film explicitly declares all existing jobs unnecessary. The moderately favorable guarantee estimate assumes that national prosperity and public infrastructure reach ordinary citizens, with a wide interval because universal entitlements are not explained.

The monarchy, royal research establishment and influential tribes keep productive power relatively concentrated. Consultation does not establish equal ownership of every advanced system. The nonworking estimate stays modest because visible prosperity is compatible with substantial useful work, including care and scientific creativity. Automated transport and advanced medical tools reduce burdens without proving a fully automatic economy. Comics constitutional details, invented fan mining systems and a canonical unemployment percentage are deliberately not asserted.

guarantees.basis: Prosperity and advanced infrastructure suggest a floor; this is an inference rather than a benefits statute.

control.basis: Royal and tribal authority outweigh evidence for equally shared productive ownership.

nonworking.basis: A conventional all-age participation scenario with continuing scientific, agricultural, craft and care work; no census.

societies.name: Marvel — Latveria under Doctor Doom
societies.society: Latveria during stable Doctor Doom rule

scope.continuity: Earth-616 comics, recurring established Doom regime
scope.period: Stable rule between major invasions and temporary depositions
exclusions: Every peasant as a leisure citizen

societies.description:
Latveria offers a paternal technological model: Doctor Doom’s inventions and robotic power support a country whose government is inseparable from its ruler. The best-guess reading is a partial automation-supported provision order, with a moderate material floor rather than universal abundance. Ordinary work and traditional settlements remain. Prosperity should not be read as political freedom, and the favorable side of the guarantee score is conditional on remaining within a stable regime that Doom chooses to maintain.

Control belongs at the concentrated human end. Robots, surveillance and automated administration extend Doom’s authority rather than replacing him with an independent AI sovereign. The participation estimate assumes that machinery reduces some necessary work but leaves farming, services, care and administration active. Neither the broad reference nor a ruler’s benevolent self-image supplies an unemployment census. Guarantees have a wide interval because dependence on one ruler can coexist with material security for compliant residents and severe vulnerability for dissidents.

guarantees.basis: A continuing technological paternalism is the best-guess model; a universal statutory floor is not established.

control.basis: Doom is the human autocrat directing technology.

nonworking.basis: Editorial all-age estimate allows machinery to reduce work while retaining substantial human farming, services and care.

societies.name: Marvel: X-Men — Krakoa

scope.period: Established Quiet Council era before the third Hellfire Gala attack
exclusions: Krakoa the island counted as an idle human

societies.description:
Krakoa supplies self-sustaining habitats and miraculous biological infrastructure while pharmaceutical exports support the mutant nation’s place in the outside economy. This is included by functional analogy to automatic production: a living engineered or mutant support system reduces residents’ dependence on ordinary wage work. It is not a literal robot factory, and the island is a sentient participant. The guarantee estimate favors resident access while recognizing gate restrictions, political exclusion and the labor involved in medical resurrection.

The Quiet Council and key providers concentrate decisions, although the benefits are shared across a much larger resident population. That combination places control between elite management and a commons, rather than automatically at the fully democratic end. A comparatively high nonworking estimate allows ordinary residents freedom from many subsistence jobs, while counting the Five, researchers, diplomats, carers and defenders as useful workers. This is a best guess about participation, not evidence that every mutant spends life at leisure.

guarantees.basis: Self-sustaining habitats and national provision support a resident floor; exact individual entitlements are inferred.

control.basis: The Quiet Council and special providers hold substantial power despite broadly shared benefits.

nonworking.basis: Editorial resident participation scenario with many freed from subsistence jobs and substantial continuing specialist/care work.

societies.name: Marvel: Spider-Man 2099 — Nueva York

scope.population: Human civilian residents of Nueva York
exclusions: Automated weapons as evidence of unlimited free food

societies.description:
Nueva York turns advanced technology into corporate power while ordinary residents remain dependent on unequal access to jobs, protection and goods. Alchemax’s engineering and automated enforcement make a useful zero-variant comparison: labor-saving capacity exists without a shared release from wage dependence. The high unfavorable guarantee score reflects this corporate dystopia. It does not invent a specific welfare prohibition or claim that every form of human labor has already become technically replaceable.

Productive control sits near concentrated human ownership, because executives and corporations direct the systems rather than an autonomous machine polity or an equal citizen collective. The modest nonworking estimate allows dependents and marginal residents while retaining widespread useful employment, informal work and care. It is a broad all-age assumption, not a comic-book labor statistic. The scope stops before Doom’s nationalization, since changing the formal owner would require a separate assessment of whether ordinary access and effective control actually changed.

guarantees.basis: Official corporate-dystopia framing supports weak guarantees; detailed benefit rules are not given.

control.basis: Alchemax executives and corporate institutions concentrate productive decisions.

nonworking.basis: All-age best guess with widespread work and a dependent/excluded minority; not a quoted unemployment rate.

societies.name: Star Wars — Geonosis’s automated hive industry
societies.society: Living Geonosian hive society during the Clone Wars

scope.continuity: Screen canon, Attack of the Clones and The Clone Wars
scope.population: Living organic Geonosians as an explicit alien-person proxy
exclusions: Universal household guarantees inferred from military output

societies.description:
Geonosis has an unmistakable automatic production system: its assembly complexes manufacture droids, weapons and vehicles at enormous scale. The best-guess admission is a partial transition in which machine output supports a living hive society, without assuming that every worker shares its gains. Guarantees stay weak because industrial power does not establish secure individual access, and the political order is hierarchical. The record ends before Imperial extermination; dead inhabitants never become a nonworking population.

Poggle’s factory authority and the queen’s deeper control place productive decisions near the concentrated organic end. The rulers are biological aliens, so the coordinate is an explicitly disclosed analogy to human elite control, not AI sovereignty. A modest nonworking estimate leaves substantial organic engineering, care, hive maintenance and military activity in view. Factory automation alone cannot fix an exact participation share or prove free food. The coordinates therefore express a bounded interpretation of the depicted industrial society rather than a complete alien economic constitution.

guarantees.basis: Automated military output does not demonstrate household entitlements; weak access is a best guess.

control.basis: Biological factory leadership and queen rule are analogous to concentrated human elite control, not AI rule.

nonworking.basis: Editorial organic-population estimate retains real engineering, care, maintenance and military work.
